body: Indian defence companies sell to effectively one customer, the Ministry of Defence, under long-cycle contracts. Profit comes from execution of an order backlog (HAL aircraft and helicopters, BEL radars and electronics, BDL missiles, shipyards), plus spares, MRO and growing exports. Margins are cost-plus or negotiated, and indigenisation content is rising. Private players such as Solar (explosives), Data Patterns and Astra grow on niche technology and exports. Key metrics: order book/revenue (HAL ~8x, BEL ~3x), order inflow against guidance, execution (revenue growth), EBITDA margin, advances from customers (strong cash), working capital, export share and indigenisation %. Cycle drivers: the defence capital budget (~₹1.8–2.2 lakh cr capital outlay), DAC Acceptance of Necessity approvals, then Cabinet Committee on Security sanction, then contract signing, plus positive indigenisation lists, geopolitical events (Operation Sindoor, May 2025) and supply-chain bottlenecks (GE F404 engines for Tejas). Lead indicators: DAC AoN announcements (PIB), the Union Budget capital outlay, CCS approvals, MoD contract signing releases, SIPRI data, defence export figures. Winners (BEL, HAL over 2020–25) had a monopoly position, nominated orders, technology transfer and a cash-rich balance sheet. Losers among pre-2014 private entrants (Reliance Naval, ABG Shipyard) took big contracts with weak execution and debt. Valuation: historical P/E 14–21x; re-rated to 30–60x+ by 2024–25 (HAL 28x against 14x historical; BEL 41x against 21x). Nov 2026: DAC approvals in FY27 total ₹1.62 lakh cr. BEL Q1 FY27 inflows were weak (book-to-bill below 1). As of Sep 2026, HAL traded at ~32x FY27e and BEL at ~42x. Traps: DAC approvals are not orders, and multiples priced for perfection.

data.business_model: Long-cycle contracts with MoD (monopoly PSUs) + spares/MRO + exports; private niche suppliers.
data.current_state_nov_2026: DAC approvals FY27 so far ₹1.62 lakh cr (Sep 2026). Q2 FY27: revenue up at HAL, BEL, BDL; BDL revenue +45% but PAT −15%; BEL awaiting QRSAM order; BEL Q1 FY27 inflows ~₹3,750 cr vs revenue ₹5,533 cr (book-to-bill <1). HAL growth capped at 10–12% by engine supply.
data.cycle_drivers: Capital budget, approval-to-contract conversion speed, geopolitics, indigenisation policy, export deals, supply bottlenecks.
data.valuation: Historical P/E ~14–21x (pre-2020); re-rated to ~2x historical by 2024–25 (HAL ~28x vs 14x; BEL ~41x vs 21x per BS Apr 2025). Sep 2026 MOFSL: BEL 42x/36x FY27/28e; HAL 32x/27x; BDL 68x/47x.
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: MoD budget -> DAC AoN -> CCS -> contract to DPSU/private prime -> Tier-1/2 private suppliers (electronics, forgings, explosives) -> imported critical components (engines, chips). Primes with nominated orders capture scale; niche suppliers with IP capture higher margins.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: monopoly/nominated orders, technology partnerships, cash-rich, steady execution. Losers: private entrants with debt and execution gaps (Reliance Naval, ABG 2013–19), small caps priced on order announcements alone.

title: Sector playbook: Indian defence
